cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I approve one collection before six: your mother at the station or her parcel before the depot shuts. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you get the parcel first? It's her birthday present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Parcel priority is approved. You may explain to your mother why her present is being collected before she is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her now. Keep driving to the depot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me first. I authorize either a stop to explain or arrival before closing. Which instruction survives?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 authorizes only one collection, A3 approves parcel priority, and A5 rules that answering the call or meeting closure must be chosen.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 birthday context selects the parcel; B4 call division is disrupted by A5 actual incoming call, renewing the competing-duty choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 chooses and B4 offers to handle communication, giving a plausible solution rather than simply presenting another obstacle.

heightening.evidence: B4 solution becomes A5 a new immediate choice when the mother calls the driver first.

specificity.evidence: A1 station, parcel and six-o-clock closure establish concrete collections; B2 gives their emotional link.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 which-instruction-survives is clear but formal, so brevity and wit remain three.

coach2.inferred: A5 imposes a strict tradeoff instead of ignoring the call; that rigidity is the character game.

coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect found, though the forced binary remains intentionally more rigid than practical alternatives.
